CausalChain: DDR gene alterations in BTC lead to genomic instability and neoantigen formation -> Neoantigen generation partially stimulates immune recognition, but is countered by an immunosuppressive TME (e.g., enhanced PD-L1 expression, presence of regulatory T cells and myeloid-derived suppressor cells) -> DDR deficiency also activates cytosolic DNA sensing (STING pathway) releasing pro-inflammatory cytokines, yet the overall effect remains suboptimal due to TME suppression -> Pharmacologically inhibiting DDR (e.g., with PARP inhibitors) together with agents that reprogram the immunosuppressive TME can amplify neoantigen presentation and restore effective immune surveillance -> This synergism can sensitize otherwise “cold” BTCs to immune checkpoint blockade.
Hypothesis: In biliary tract cancer, tumors harboring DDR pathway deficiencies—even in the context of low MSI and moderate TMB—can be rendered more immunoresponsive through a dual therapeutic strategy that combines DDR inhibitors with agents targeting the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, thereby enhancing neoantigen-driven immune activation and improving the efficacy of immune checkpoint inhibitors.
Abstract: Biliary tract cancers (BTCs) are characterized by modest responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs), in part due to a generally immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) and low prevalence of classical predictive biomarkers such as high microsatellite instability (MSI-H). Recent studies have highlighted that defects in the DNA damage repair (DDR) pathway are present in a subset of BTCs and can drive genomic instability and the generation of neoantigens, but often fail to fully activate the antitumor immune response due to concurrent recruitment of suppressive immune cells. We propose that the interplay between DDR deficiency‐induced neoantigen load and the immunosuppressive TME represents a critical axis that can be exploited for therapeutic gain. Specifically, combining DDR inhibitors with agents that modulate the TME may potentiate the immunogenicity of BTCs and enhance response to ICIs.
